images.title: The paper fan at three places
images.purpose: Show the angle the two end sticks of a paper fan make at three places, X, Y and Z, and name them right, acute and obtuse by comparing with a quarter turn.
images.composition: Three equal panels in a row, each with a teal fixed stick, an amber turning stick, a green folded-paper wedge between them and a red arc marking the angle.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Three panels, each 420 by 520 px with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and a very pale cream #FFF8E7 fill, at x 50 to 470, x 518 to 938 and x 986 to 1406, all y 130 to 650. In every panel the two sticks meet at the fan's corner, a dark dot 22 px across: panel X at (110, 560), panel Y at (578, 560), panel Z at (1046, 560). The fixed stick is teal #0072B2 (10 px line, 280 px long) going right from the corner along y 560. The turning stick is amber #E69F00 (10 px line, 280 px long). Between the two sticks a flat green #009E73 folded-paper wedge with 8 thin dark fold lines (a circular sector of radius 240 px) fills the angle. A red #D55E00 arc (4 px, radius 80 px) marks the angle at the corner. Panel X: the turning stick goes straight up (a quarter turn, with a small square corner mark 36 by 36 px). Panel Y: the turning stick goes up and to the right so that the angle is clearly narrower than a square corner (the stick ends at about (578 plus 280 times 0.87, 560 minus 280 times 0.5), (821, 420)). Panel Z: the turning stick goes up and to the left so that the angle is clearly wider than a square corner but less than a straight line (the stick ends at about (1046 minus 140, 560 minus 242), (906, 318)). The letters X, Y and Z sit above the panels at y 180 (50 px, bold, dark). Captions under the panels, centred at y 700 in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (34 px, bold): right angle under X, acute angle under Y and obtuse angle under Z; and a second line at y 740 (30 px): a quarter turn under X, less than a quarter turn under Y and more than a quarter turn under Z. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
sticks of different lengths in the three panels
any fraction written anywhere in the frame
images.takeaway: A quarter turn makes a right angle, less than a quarter turn an acute angle and more than a quarter turn an obtuse angle.
images.description: A paper fan at three places: a quarter turn (right angle), less than a quarter turn (acute angle) and more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn (obtuse angle).
images.context: Concept image for Right, Acute and Obtuse Angles. It follows the idea of the paper fan and the straws in your maths book and shows the concept's own example of a fan at three places, X, Y and Z.
images.teaching_notes: Compare each angle with the square corner of a book. The slip to watch is thinking a longer stick makes a bigger angle.

image_decisions.why: The fan at three places shows right, acute and obtuse angles side by side against the same quarter turn.
